steps.note: the sample recording, wide, framed the way it was captured. The panel has a Reframe section saying Scale 100%, the middle of the picture in the middle of the frame, and one line saying it is framed the same way for its whole length

THE FIRST TEST: where it pushes in to is POINTED AT, not typed. A box dragged round the tile in the recording, the one thing in it worth looking at, with the playhead on the moment that part matters. The panel's hint now says what Punch In will do with it, and Punch In has come alive

THE SECOND TEST: the camera ARRIVED at the playhead. One press and the canvas is already showing what was pointed at, filling the frame, because the move leaned in over the second before this moment rather than setting off from it. The box is gone: it said what it had to say. Two lanes appeared on the timing strip, Scale and Position, because a punch-in is those two properties and not a zoom tool

back at the first frame and the picture is wide again. Nothing was baked in: the framing is worked out for whatever moment is on screen, the same bargain every other piece of styling in the app strikes

THE THIRD TEST: it HELD. Well past the move, with nothing asked for and nothing keyed, the frame has not budged off what it was pointed at. A hold is what a property does after its last key, so nobody has to ask for one

THE FOURTH TEST: pull back out, setting off from the playhead. Everything between the punch-in's last key and this one is now the hold, and it was never asked for. The Scale lane on the strip runs from the first move to this one as a single bar, because it is one property with four keys on it rather than two motions fighting over one answer
and at the end it is wide again, on the whole picture, exactly where it started
Reset gives the whole frame back and takes both lanes off the strip. Every one of these is an ordinary history step
one press of undo and the move is back, at the size it had landed on. Nothing here has its own undo stack
